input_signals.name: R&D-Addback Liability Power
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with strong earnings after adding back expensed R&D are accounting-distressed rather than economically fragile.
input_signals.reasoning: Traditional earnings understate profitability for firms that expense productive knowledge investment. Conditioning the R&D intensity on R&D-adjusted income relative to liabilities favors firms whose apparent distress is driven by accounting treatment, not inability to service obligations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( xrd, sale ) ), rank( ratio( add( ib, xrd ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Cash-Burn Leverage Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(xrd, intan), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(NEG(oancf), at), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible-heavy firms with negative operating cash flow and high debt are genuinely fragile and should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Productive intangible assets do not protect shareholders if the firm is burning cash while carrying substantial financial obligations. This interaction penalizes firms where intangible intensity coincides with funding stress rather than masking it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( xrd, intan ), at ) ), sumrank( ratio( neg( oancf ), at ), ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Gross-Surplus Liability Cover
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with strong gross operating surplus relative to liabilities are more likely to be accounting-distressed than truly fragile.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the accrual-style cash-minus-earnings leg with a pre-discretionary-spending measure of economic surplus. If an R&D-heavy firm generates strong gross profits before expensed knowledge investment, weak bottom-line accounting profitability is less likely to indicate inability to support liabilities.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Liability-Growth Spiral
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUMRANK(GROWTH(lt, 1), NEG(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with expanding liabilities and deteriorating gross surplus are genuinely fragile and should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Rising obligations are especially dangerous when knowledge investment is not translating into improving operating surplus. This focuses on a dynamic financing spiral rather than a static leverage screen, identifying intangible-heavy firms whose distress is worsening rather than merely accounting-based.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), sumrank( growth( lt, 1 ), neg( growth( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D-Adjusted Loss Liability Spiral
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(pi, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), GROWTH(lt, 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms that remain unprofitable even after adding back R&D while liabilities are growing are genuinely fragile and should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: The R&D addback separates accounting losses caused by expensing knowledge investment from losses that persist even after adjustment. Pairing adjusted losses with liability growth targets firms where distress is worsening rather than merely mismeasured.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), sumrank( neg( ratio( add( pi, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ), growth( lt, 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Goodwill Equity-Cushion Cash Burn
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose equity cushion is heavily dependent on goodwill and whose operations are burning cash relative to liabilities should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Goodwill becomes especially dangerous when it represents a large share of the effective equity cushion, because impairment can quickly erode book solvency. Cash burn relative to liabilities distinguishes this from a harmless accounting composition issue and points to genuine financing pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( winsor( ratio( gdwl, add( gdwl, ceq ) ), 1 ) ), rank( ratio( neg( oancf ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Accumulated-Deficit Repair
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with improving retained earnings are resolving accounting distress rather than drifting toward financial failure.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from gross-surplus liability coverage and instead tests whether accumulated accounting deficits are being repaired over time. For intangible-heavy firms, retained earnings can be depressed by expensed R&D, so improvement in retained earnings-to-assets is evidence that knowledge investment is becoming self-sustaining.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( delta( ratio( re, at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent R&D Cash-Flow Floor
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with persistent R&D programs and a stable lower bound on operating cash flow should outperform because their intangible investment is financeable through downturns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the internal-versus-goodwill normalization tweak with a different mechanism: persistence of knowledge investment conditioned on downside cash-flow resilience. A high R&D firm whose worst recent cash-flow outcome remains strong is less likely to be genuinely distressed, even if accounting earnings look weak.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 5 ) ), rank( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Knowledge Working-Capital Stability
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent R&D firms with stable working-capital positions are less likely to be experiencing genuine liquidity distress and should outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids claiming that working-capital deficits are inherently good; instead it rewards stability in the liquidity base supporting intangible investment. For knowledge-intensive firms, stable working capital suggests the firm can maintain operations and R&D without recurring liquidity shocks.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 3 ) ), rank( neg( vol( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Tax-Paying R&D Solvency
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms paying meaningful taxes relative to liabilities are more likely to have real taxable profitability despite accounting measures that may make them appear distressed.
input_signals.reasoning: Tax expense provides an external validation channel distinct from gross surplus, accruals, or cash-flow addbacks. If a firm invests heavily in expensed knowledge capital yet still generates taxable income, traditional accounting distress measures may overstate its financial fragility.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( txt, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Maturity-Matched Financing
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with liabilities tilted away from near-term debt maturities should outperform because their knowledge investment has more time to mature.
input_signals.reasoning: R&D assets are long-duration and hard to pledge, so short-term debt creates rollover risk before the investment payoff arrives. A larger long-term-versus-current debt mix reduces the chance that accounting distress becomes binding financial distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( dltt, dlc ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Capitalized Intangible Turnover Stress
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(intan, at)), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(sale, at), 5)), NEG(RATIO(oancf, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high capitalized intangibles, weak asset turnover relative to their own history, and poor operating cash-flow coverage of liabilities are likely holding impaired or stranded intangible assets.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the unstable sale-to-intangibles denominator by measuring commercial productivity as sales relative to total assets and ranking it against the firm’s own history. Weak cash-flow coverage of liabilities confirms that low intangible productivity is financially relevant rather than merely an accounting mix issue.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( intan, at ) ), sumrank( neg( ts_rank( ratio( sale, at ), 5 ) ), neg( ratio( oancf, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Financed Goodwill Accretion
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms adding goodwill while liabilities rise and retained earnings deteriorate are more likely to have made debt-financed acquisitions that fail to create economic value.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts from the static goodwill-times-low-profitability-times-leverage template to a dynamic acquisition-quality mechanism. Rising goodwill is most concerning when accompanied by liability growth and worsening accumulated profitability, suggesting overpayment, integration failure, or future impairment risk.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), sumrank( growth( lt, 1 ), neg( delta( ratio( re, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Adjusted Net-Income Recovery
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with improving R&D-adjusted net income should outperform because their apparent accounting distress is being resolved by productive knowledge investment.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the 5-year floor template with a recovery mechanism based on change in adjusted profitability. Adding back R&D addresses accounting expensing, while improvement in adjusted net income indicates that the firm is moving away from genuine operating fragility rather than merely showing a stable historical minimum.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( delta( ratio( add( ni, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Goodwill Working-Capital Integration Strain
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms adding goodwill while working capital deteriorates are more likely experiencing acquisition-integration strain and should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the static goodwill-load, thin-equity, cash-burn construction and instead tests a dynamic post-acquisition balance-sheet strain. Rising goodwill can be benign, but if working capital weakens at the same time, the acquisition may be consuming liquidity or failing to convert into operating resilience.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( wcap, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Ranked R&D Tax-Cash Coverage
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(txt, lt)), RANK(RATIO(oancf, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with both tax-validated profitability and operating cash-flow coverage of liabilities should outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Ranking the tax and cash channels before multiplying avoids the original MIN scale problem where the smaller tax ratio dominated the signal. The interaction requires dual confirmation that the intangible-heavy firm can support liabilities through both taxable earnings and operating cash generation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), mul( rank( ratio( txt, lt ) ), rank( ratio( oancf, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Goodwill Tax-Validation Deterioration
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms adding goodwill while tax-validated profitability deteriorates are more likely experiencing poor acquisition quality and should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the accruals-minus-tax construction and no longer overlaps mechanically with the noncash-earnings-quality gap. Goodwill accretion is most concerning when the acquired asset base is followed by declining tax profitability, suggesting weaker real earnings capacity and greater impairment risk.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( txt, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Gross-Profit Cash-Quality Floor
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), MUL(RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5)), RANK(RATIO(che, act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent R&D firms with durable gross-profit capacity and cash-heavy current assets are more likely to be accounting-distressed than genuinely fragile.
input_signals.reasoning: The multi-year gross-profit floor asks whether the firm has maintained an economic surplus before expensed knowledge investment. Cash as a share of current assets provides a liquidity-quality filter, favoring firms whose current assets can actually support continued R&D through stress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 3 ) ), mul( rank( ts_min( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 5 ) ), rank( ratio( che, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Revenue-Obligation Scale
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent R&D firms with revenue scale large relative to current liabilities should outperform because commercialization capacity reduces the likelihood that accounting distress becomes binding financial distress.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the criticized cash-runway construction with a top-line commercialization-versus-obligation mechanism. The signal asks whether the firm has enough operating scale to support near-term claims while continuing knowledge investment, rather than reusing cash plus short-debt coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 3 ) ), rank( ratio( sale, lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Retained-Equity Quality
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent R&D firms whose equity base is supported by retained earnings rather than external equity dependence should outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This addresses the ambiguity in changes in book equity by focusing on the composition and quality of the equity cushion. For intangible-heavy firms, retained earnings support indicates that prior R&D has generated cumulative profitability, reducing the chance that solvency improvement is merely issuance-funded.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 3 ) ), rank( ratio( re, add( abs( re ), abs( ceq ) ) ) ) )
